name: Formstack Forms
tagline: Build a secure low-volume form workflow with approvals and exports

pricing.notes: Typical entry Forms monthly package; enterprise packaging can vary.

tiers.name: Forms
tiers.limits: 1 form builder, 25 forms, 1,000 submissions per form, and 2GB storage

tiers.name: Suite
tiers.limits: 3 form builders, 100 forms, 5,000 submissions per form, 10GB storage, unlimited document senders and unlimited e-signature senders

tiers.name: Salesforce Solutions
tiers.limits: Salesforce-native forms, documents and signatures; limits and price are custom

tiers.name: Enterprise
tiers.limits: Unlimited users and submissions; other allowances and commercial terms are custom

pricing.billingTerms: monthly + annual (annual is approximately 2 months free)
pricing.hiddenCosts: Additional users, submissions and features cost extra at unpublished rates; HIPAA compliance is a paid add-on on Forms and Suite.

verdictSummary: A consolation build is possible, but the paid product's decisive value sits outside a solo rebuild. For Formstack Forms, build a secure low-volume form workflow with approvals and exports. The hard boundary is enterprise compliance, workflow, integrations, support, and regulated deployments, plus integrations, deliverability, and workflow depth.
coreLoopDIY: Build a secure low-volume public form workflow with approvals, validate submissions, notify the owner, and provide a private response table with CSV export.
requirements: Resend API key or SMTP credentials
whatYouLose: enterprise compliance, workflow, integrations, support, and regulated deployments
ongoingBurden: spam control, email delivery, storage, exports, accessibility, conditional logic, and integrations
whyPeopleStillPay: People still pay for Formstack Forms because a basic form is trivial; people pay when the form feeds a dependable business workflow and never loses a response. The recurring cost buys spam control, email delivery, storage, exports, accessibility, conditional logic, and integrations, not just the visible interface.

priorArt.name: Formbricks
priorArt.desc: Active open-source survey and experience-management platform.

alternatives.name: Budibase
alternatives.desc: Forms, approvals, and automations in one box; you supply the box

rejectedAlternatives.name: NocoDB
rejectedAlternatives.desc: Community forms are usable, but conditional fields, validation, redirects, and the richer workflow layer are paid

notes: Editorial comparison targets the Forms plan and a single-owner form service DIY substitute. Recheck price before merge.
prompt:
Build a closest honest personal substitute for Formstack Forms in an empty repository.
Use Next.js 15, TypeScript, Tailwind CSS, SQLite, Drizzle ORM, and Resend; do not offer alternative stacks.
The core loop is: build a secure low-volume public form workflow with approvals, validate submissions, notify the owner, and provide a private response table with CSV export.
Make the first run work locally with one documented command.
Store all user data locally by default and make export straightforward.
Put secrets in .env, ship .env.example, and never commit credentials.
Create a form builder with short text, long text, email, number, select, radio, checkbox, and file fields.
Publish each form at a stable slug with server-side validation and accessible labels.
Add honeypot, rate limiting, submission-size limits, and a clear privacy notice.
Store responses in SQLite and provide search, filters, detail view, and CSV export.
Send an owner notification without placing submitted values in logs.
Support a thank-you screen and one simple conditional branch.
Include clear empty, loading, success, and recoverable error states.
Add input validation, safe filenames, and graceful handling of unavailable APIs.
Write focused tests for the core transformation and one end-to-end happy path.
Create a README with setup, architecture, permissions, data location, and backup steps.
Do not add accounts, billing, telemetry, analytics, or a hosted control plane.
Do not claim to reproduce proprietary data, network liquidity, regulated access, or frontier infrastructure.
Deliberately leave out payment collection.
Deliberately leave out hundreds of third-party integrations.
Deliberately leave out multi-brand enterprise workspaces and compliance attestations.
Finish by running the tests and listing the exact commands used.
